sop_modules.name: Setup — Landscape/Hardscape Ground Protection, Fixture Masking, Fascia Edge Protection, Vent Masking, Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Full setup module for exterior soffit repaint. Ground protection below soffit work zone is CRITICAL — overhead work sends all drips and scraping debris straight down via gravity. Landscape and hardscape protection must be in place before any overhead work begins. Fascia edge masking is MANDATORY in RP (fascia is almost always already finished — unlike NC where fascia may be unfinished). Vent opening masking prevents further paint clogging during brush_roll application on vented soffit. Equipment setup includes ladders/scaffold per access tier and extension poles for overhead roller work.

tasks.name: Landscape Ground Protection Below Soffit
tasks.description: Deploy plastic sheeting and tarps over landscape areas directly below soffit work zone. CRITICAL for overhead RP — gravity pulls all drips, roller spatter, scraping debris, and overspray straight down. Brush/roll: edge tarps at base covering full drip fallout zone. Spray (non-vented): full tarp coverage over entire drip zone. RRP: upgrade to 6-mil poly. Wider coverage than vertical surface protection because overhead debris spreads further.
tasks.notes: Shared zone with SF_TRIM_EXT_RP — first spec in elevation sequence owns setup. Cross-spec deduplication rule U-004. RP emphasis: catches scraping debris in addition to drips.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_LANDSCAPE_PROTECT (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Hardscape Walkway Protection Below Soffit
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over walkways and hardscape directly below soffit work area. Non-slip canvas for crew traffic areas. Upgrade to full_cover for spray or RRP.
tasks.notes: Shared zone with SF_TRIM_EXT_RP — cross-spec deduplication rule U-004.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_HARDSCAPE_PROTECT (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Soffit Light Fixture Masking
tasks.description: Mask soffit-mounted light fixtures — recessed lights, porch fixtures. Bag and tape or remove cover plate where accessible. Mandatory in RP — fixtures are installed and operational.
tasks.notes: RP: all fixtures are installed and operational — masking is mandatory.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_FIXTURE_MASK (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Fascia Edge Masking
tasks.description: Apply tape and 12-inch masking film along fascia-soffit junction to protect finished fascia from overhead roller spatter, scraping debris, and spray overspray. In RP, fascia is almost always already painted — masking is MANDATORY regardless of application method.
tasks.notes: RP: fascia is almost always already finished. Mandatory for both brush_roll and spray methods. NC version was conditional on fascia being finished; RP version is unconditional.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_FASCIA_MASK (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Mask Soffit Vent Openings (Vented Soffit Only)
tasks.description: Apply tape or foam plugs to individual soffit vent openings before brush_roll application. Prevents further paint accumulation in vents from RP coating (FM-006). Vented soffit only — non-vented soffit has no openings. RP-specific concern: prior coats may have partially clogged vents, and each repaint adds more blockage.
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC. Vent masking adds ~5% labor to brush_roll on vented soffit. Spray is PROHIBITED on vented soffit, so no spray vent masking needed.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup for Overhead Work
tasks.description: Set up ladders or scaffold per access_type. Stage extension poles for overhead roller application, brushes, roller trays, and materials. Extension pole is the primary overhead tool — reduces fatigue and improves coverage consistency.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per session. Includes ladder/scaffold positioning per access tier.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_EQUIPMENT_SETUP_BRUSH (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup for Overhead Work
tasks.description: Set up ladders or scaffold per access_type. Configure airless sprayer with 413-515 tip for overhead soffit application. Lower pressure settings for overhead work to control overspray. NON-VENTED SOFFIT ONLY.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per session. Spray PROHIBITED on vented soffit (FM-001).
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_EQUIPMENT_SETUP_SPRAY (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape/hardscape ground protection first → Fixture and fascia masking → Vent masking (vented soffit + brush_roll only) → Equipment setup last. ALL ground protection must be in place before any overhead work begins.

sop_modules.name: Condition Assessment — Visual Inspect, Adhesion Test, Mildew Assess, Moisture Check, Caulk Assess, Vent Condition
sop_modules.description: RP-specific condition assessment module. Six-point assessment drives all downstream task activation: (1) Visual condition inspection with DSD rating and condition_scale assignment (GOOD/FAIR/POOR). (2) ASTM D3359 adhesion test — pass = skip full prime, fail = full prime required. (3) Mildew/algae assessment — soffit-specific PRIORITY CHECK because mildew is the #1 degradation mechanism on sheltered overhead surfaces. (4) Moisture probe on wood panels at joints and near roof penetrations. (5) Caulk condition assessment at panel joints and soffit-to-trim junctions per 'Think Like a Water Drop'. (6) Vent condition check for paint clogging from prior coats. All assessment is FIXED time per 100 SF of soffit. 100% RP_NEW tasks.

tasks.name: Visual Condition Inspection — All Soffit Surfaces
tasks.description: Scan all soffit surfaces from ladder/scaffold at working height. Map cracking, peeling, adhesion failure, chalking, fading, moisture staining, and paint film buildup. Assign condition_scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) based on worst-condition area per worst-state-wins rule. Photograph defects. Document scope of scraping, feathering, and treatment needed. Overhead inspection requires good lighting — headlamp or portable light angled to reveal defects.

quality_notes.QT2: Standard visual scan, document visible defects
quality_notes.QT3: Thorough scan with work light, document all defect areas, per-elevation assessment
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan with raking light overhead, photograph all defects, per-panel assessment

tasks.notes: Soffit condition is typically GOOD or FAIR when repaint occurs due to sheltered location. POOR condition concentrated at moisture intrusion points.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
tasks.description: Perform cross-hatch tape test per ASTM D3359 at representative soffit sections. Test at minimum 2 locations per elevation. Results determine if full prime or spot prime is required. Pass + SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT = skip full prime (ROUND_SFRP_2FINISH). Fail = full prime required regardless of visual condition.
tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED time. Adhesion test is critical for soffit — sheltered location means coating may appear sound but have adhesion failure from moisture migration through vent openings.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Mildew/Algae Assessment — Soffit-Specific Priority Check
tasks.description: Inspect all soffit surfaces for mildew (dark spots/patches) and algae (green/yellow growth). Classify extent: spot (<25%), moderate (25-50%), widespread (>50%). Mildew is the #1 degradation mechanism on sheltered overhead soffit — shaded, damp conditions under eaves are ideal for biological growth. North-facing soffits and poorly ventilated eave cavities are highest risk. Results drive biocide treatment scope in prep module.
tasks.notes: Soffit-specific priority assessment. Mildew MUST be killed before painting — painting over mildew = guaranteed adhesion failure.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Moisture Check — Panel Joints, Roof Penetrations
tasks.description: Moisture meter reading on wood soffit panels at joints, near roof penetrations, and at water staining locations. Soffit moisture comes from ABOVE (attic condensation, roof leaks) rather than from weather exposure. MC > 15% is STOP WORK for coating on that area until moisture source is resolved and wood dries to <12%.
tasks.notes: Wood soffit only. Fiber cement and vinyl do not absorb moisture the same way. Per-elevation FIXED time.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Caulk Condition Assessment — Panel Joints and Trim Junctions
tasks.description: Inspect all existing caulk at soffit panel-to-panel joints, soffit-to-fascia junction, soffit-to-frieze junction, and soffit-to-corner board junction per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol. Classify: intact and flexible (paint over), cracked or separated (remove and replace), fully failed (remove all, re-caulk). Soffit caulk failures are common at panel joints due to thermal expansion/contraction cycling.
tasks.notes: Caulk at soffit-to-fascia and soffit-to-frieze junctions is THIS spec's responsibility (not trim spec). Results drive caulk repair scope in prep module.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Vent Opening Condition Check (Vented Soffit Only)
tasks.description: Inspect soffit vent openings for paint clogging from prior brush_roll applications. Classify: clear (no action), partially clogged (clean in prep), heavily clogged (note for homeowner — vent replacement outside painting scope). RP-specific concern: each repaint cycle adds paint accumulation in vents, reducing attic ventilation over time.
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC. Vented soffit only. Non-vented soffit has no vent openings — skip.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Visual condition inspection first → Mildew/algae assessment (soffit-specific priority) → Adhesion test → Moisture check (wood only) → Caulk assessment → Vent condition check (vented only). Assessment results determine which prep and prime tasks activate downstream.

sop_modules.name: Prep — Low-Pressure Wash, Mildew Treatment, Chalk Remediation, Scrape/Feather, Degloss/Scuff, Caulk Repair, Vent Clean, Substrate-Specific Spot Scuff, Dust Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Condition-driven prep module for exterior soffit repaint. Low-pressure wash per elevation (500-800 PSI max — NEVER power wash soffit). Mildew/algae biocide treatment (soffit-specific critical task — #1 failure mode prevention). Chalk remediation for SS_EXT_CHALKING. Scrape and feather failing/peeling areas (overhead scraping is extremely slow — gravity works against tool stroke). Degloss/scuff sound existing paint. Caulk assess + repair at panel joints and trim junctions. Vent opening cleaning on paint-clogged vents. Substrate-specific spot scuff on exposed areas. Condition modifiers: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x on prep tasks. SF-based rates with condition/access/vent/T&G/RRP modifiers.

tasks.name: Low-Pressure Wash Soffit Surface (Per Elevation)
tasks.description: Low-pressure wash (500-800 PSI max, fan tip) all soffit surfaces on the elevation with mildew-removal detergent. Removes dirt, cobwebs, mildew residue, chalk residue, loose paint chips. HIGH-PRESSURE POWER WASHING IS PROHIBITED on soffit — damages thin panel edges, strips existing paint, forces water into attic through vent openings (COMPAT-SFIT-010). Allow 24-48 hr dry time. Per-elevation FIXED task.
tasks.notes: Per-elevation FIXED time. Cross-spec deduplication rule U-003: skip if wash already performed by another spec on same elevation. Lower PSI than trim/siding wash (500-800 vs 500-1000) due to panel edge sensitivity. Soffit dries slower than vertical surfaces — limited airflow.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_WASH_LOW_PRESSURE — RP washes existing painted surface with mildew detergent, per-elevation FIXED vs per-SF

tasks.name: Mildew/Algae Biocide Treatment
tasks.description: Apply biocide/mildewcide solution (sodium hypochlorite or commercial mildew remover) to mildew or algae-affected soffit areas. Allow full contact/kill time per product directions. Scrub with soft brush to loosen dead growth. Rinse and allow dry before priming. Soffit is the #1 exterior surface for mildew growth due to sheltered, shaded, damp conditions under eaves. Treatment is NON-NEGOTIABLE before any coating — painting over mildew = guaranteed adhesion failure.
tasks.notes: Soffit-specific critical task — mildew is the dominant degradation mechanism. North-facing elevations and poorly ventilated eaves are highest risk. Biocide dwell time: 15-30 min per manufacturer directions.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Chalk Remediation (Pre-Treatment for Chalk-Binding Primer)
tasks.description: Pre-treat chalking soffit surfaces before chalk-binding primer application. Power wash (already done) loosens heavy chalk; follow with chemical chalk remover on stubborn areas. Wipe and verify — white cloth test should show minimal residual chalk after treatment. Residual chalk will be bound by chalk-binding primer. Chalking is LESS common on soffit than other exterior surfaces (sheltered from direct UV) but occurs on south-facing soffits and eave-edge transitions.
tasks.notes: SS_EXT_CHALKING only. Chalk-binding primer (SYS_EXT_SFRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND) follows this task in prime module.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Scrape Failing Paint and Feather Edges — Overhead
tasks.description: Scrape all failing, peeling, flaking, or loose paint from soffit surfaces (panel field, panel joints, trim junctions). Feather-sand all scrape edges with 80-120 grit to create smooth transition. Overhead scraping is extremely slow — gravity works against the tool stroke and debris falls onto the painter. Panel edges are fragile — aggressive scraping can damage T&G joints, fiber cement edges, or vinyl panel locking mechanisms. Non-negotiable feathering at all tiers. Collect scraping debris for cleanup (RRP: into containment).

quality_notes.QT2: Remove all failing paint, feather edges — no visible ridge at 10 ft
quality_notes.QT3: Comprehensive scrape + feathering — no visible ridge at 6 ft
quality_notes.QT4: Thorough scrape + near-invisible feathering — smooth to touch at arm's length

tasks.notes: Condition-driven intensity: FAIR = moderate scraping (15-30% of surface); POOR = heavy scraping (40-60%+). RRP doubles scraping time (wet methods required, FAC_SFRP_RRP = 2.0x). Overhead execution makes this the slowest exterior prep task per SF.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Degloss/Scuff Existing Paint — Overhead
tasks.description: Chemical degloss (liquid sander wipe-on) or mechanical scuff (150-180 grit) on all previously painted soffit surfaces with sound adhesion. Creates adhesion profile for primer or finish coat. Chemical degloss preferred for T&G grooves and panel joints that sanding blocks cannot reach. For GOOD condition (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT), degloss/scuff may be the only prep task needed.

quality_notes.QT3: Full surface degloss — chemical or mechanical on all accessible surfaces overhead
quality_notes.QT4: Complete degloss with adhesion verification. T&G grooves hand-deglossed.

tasks.notes: Skip for SS_EXT_PEELING (full scrape renders degloss redundant). Skip for SS_EXT_CHALKING (chalk remediation + chalk-binding primer path). T&G panel_type increases degloss time (FAC_SFIT_TG_JOINTS = 1.20x).
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_SAND_PREP_WOOD — NC sands bare wood; RP degloss/scuffs existing paint

tasks.name: Assess and Repair Failed Caulk — Panel Joints and Trim Junctions
tasks.description: Based on assessment results (TSK_SFRP_ASSESS_CAULK), remove and replace cracked, shrunk, or failed caulk sections with exterior-grade paintable caulk (polyurethane or hybrid MS polymer — NEVER silicone). Caulk at soffit panel-to-panel joints, soffit-to-fascia junction, and soffit-to-frieze junction. Caulk at these junctions is THIS spec's responsibility. Allow 2-4 hr cure before painting. Overhead caulking is slower — gravity pulls caulk from the bead.

quality_notes.QT2: Replace visibly failed sections — cracked or separated joints
quality_notes.QT3: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect and failed joints, smooth tool
quality_notes.QT4: Replace all joints not in perfect condition, precision tooled bead overhead

tasks.notes: Rate varies by condition: GOOD = near-zero additional time; FAIR = moderate repair; POOR = extensive repair. Caulk AFTER primer for best adhesion (COMPAT-SFIT-009 — sequenced after prime in field execution).
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW — replaces NC TSK_SFIT_CAULK_JOINTS (fresh caulk at all joints) with condition-driven assessment and repair

tasks.name: Clean Paint-Clogged Vent Openings (Vented Soffit Only)
tasks.description: Clean partially clogged soffit vent openings with wire brush or pick to restore airflow. RP-specific task: prior brush_roll applications accumulate paint in vent perforations over multiple repaint cycles, reducing attic ventilation. Heavily clogged vents requiring replacement are outside painting scope — note on assessment for homeowner.
tasks.notes: RP-SPECIFIC. Vented soffit only. Triggered by TSK_SFRP_ASSESS_VENT finding partial clogging.
tasks.transfer_source: RP_NEW

tasks.name: Scuff-Sand Exposed Fiber Cement Areas
tasks.description: Scuff-sand exposed bare fiber cement areas (where paint has failed/peeled) with 150 grit for mechanical adhesion profile before alkali-resistant spot primer. Only on areas where scraping has revealed bare fiber cement substrate. Overhead execution.
tasks.notes: Spot task — only on exposed bare FC areas, not full surface. Prepares for SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ALKALI spot prime in prime module.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_SAND_PREP_FC — NC scuff-sands full factory surface; RP targets exposed areas only

tasks.name: Scuff-Sand Exposed Vinyl Areas
tasks.description: Scuff-sand exposed bare vinyl areas (where paint has failed/peeled) with 220 grit for mechanical adhesion profile before bonding spot primer. Only on areas where scraping has revealed bare vinyl substrate. Without scuff-sanding, bonding primer alone is insufficient — coating peels in sheets (RISK-SFIT-007).
tasks.notes: Spot task — only on exposed bare vinyl areas. Prepares for SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_BONDING spot prime in prime module.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_SAND_PREP_VINYL — NC scuff-sands full factory surface; RP targets exposed areas only

tasks.name: Prep Dust Cleanup — Overhead
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust, scraping debris, and degloss residue from soffit surface before coating. Tack cloth overhead — most dust falls away from surface when working overhead, but residual particles must be removed for adhesion. RRP: use HEPA vacuum instead of blowing.
tasks.notes: All dust and debris removed. Surface ready for primer or finish application.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_DUST_CLEANUP (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Low-pressure wash per elevation → 24-48 hr dry time → Mildew biocide treatment (if present) → Chalk remediation (if SS_EXT_CHALKING) → Scrape/feather (if FAIR/POOR) → Degloss/scuff (if GOOD/FAIR) → Scuff exposed FC/vinyl (if substrate exposed) → Vent clean (vented only) → Dust cleanup → Caulk repair (sequenced AFTER prime in field per COMPAT-SFIT-009). All prep must be complete and dry before prime.

sop_modules.name: Prime — State-Driven Primer (Brush/Roll or Spray) + Substrate-Specific Spot Primer on Exposed Areas
sop_modules.description: State-driven primer module for soffit repaint. General primer product determined by substrate STATE: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT with verified adhesion = SKIP prime (ROUND_SFRP_2FINISH). SS_EXT_CHALKING = chalk-binding primer full surface (SYS_EXT_SFRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND). SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/PEELING = acrylic stain-block primer spot or full (SYS_EXT_SFRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC_RP). Substrate-specific SPOT primer on exposed areas where paint has failed: bare wood = acrylic (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ACRYLIC), bare fiber cement = alkali-resistant (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ALKALI), bare vinyl = bonding (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_BONDING). Brush_roll or spray (non-vented only). Spray PROHIBITED on vented soffit.

tasks.name: State-Driven Primer — Brush/Roll Overhead Application
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer by brush and roller with extension pole overhead. Primer product varies by substrate state: chalk-binding (SYS_EXT_SFRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND) for SS_EXT_CHALKING (full surface), acrylic stain-block (SYS_EXT_SFRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC_RP) for SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/PEELING (spot or full based on extent). Brush for fascia/frieze junctions and T&G grooves, roller with extension pole for open field. Default method for all vented soffits.
tasks.notes: Skip for SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion verified (ROUND_SFRP_2FINISH or ROUND_SFRP_1FINISH). State drives product selection; application is identical.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_PRIME_BRUSH_ROLL — NC uses substrate-specific primer on full bare surface; RP uses state-driven primer

tasks.name: State-Driven Primer — Spray Overhead Application (Non-Vented Only)
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer by airless spray overhead. NON-VENTED SOFFIT ONLY — spray on vented soffit drives paint into attic through perforations (FM-001). Lower pressure settings for overhead application to control overspray fallout. Primer product varies by substrate state.
tasks.notes: Skip for SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion verified. Spray requires full adjacent masking.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_PRIME_SPRAY — NC uses substrate-specific primer via spray; RP uses state-driven primer via spray

tasks.name: Spot Prime Exposed Fiber Cement with Alkali-Resistant Primer
tasks.description: Brush-apply alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_ALKALI) to exposed bare fiber cement areas where paint has failed/peeled. Spot priming only — targets areas where scraping has revealed bare fiber cement substrate (pH 13.0 — standard acrylic primer causes saponification). Brush only — spot application too small for spray.
tasks.notes: Cladding-specific spot prime. Applied IN ADDITION to general state-driven prime (not instead of). Brush only regardless of finish method.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_PRIME_ALKALI_BRUSH_ROLL — NC primes full bare FC surface; RP spot primes exposed areas only

tasks.name: Spot Prime Exposed Vinyl with Bonding Primer
tasks.description: Brush-apply bonding primer (SYS_EXT_SFIT_PRIMER_BONDING) to exposed bare vinyl areas where paint has failed/peeled. Spot priming only — targets areas where scraping has revealed bare vinyl substrate. Standard primers will NOT bond to vinyl — bonding primer is mandatory. Recoat within 1 week or primer loses flexibility (RISK-SFIT-008). Brush only — spot application too small for spray.
tasks.notes: Cladding-specific spot prime. Standard primers will NOT bond to vinyl. Recoat within 1 week. Brush only regardless of finish method.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_SFIT_PRIME_VINYL_BRUSH_ROLL — NC primes full vinyl surface; RP spot primes exposed areas only

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Substrate-specific spot prime first (alkali on exposed FC, bonding on exposed vinyl), then general state-driven prime coat (chalk-binding or acrylic stain-block). Spot prime addresses exposed substrate chemistry; general prime addresses overall condition. Module SKIPPED entirely when SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT with verified adhesion. Allow full dry per product specs before interstage or finish.

sop_modules.name: Interstage — Intercoat Inspection, Sand, Touch-Up, Dust Removal
sop_modules.description: Between-coat inspection and maintenance for soffit repaint. Inspect first finish coat overhead, sand between coats at QT4 (220 grit overhead), touch up defects, dust removal. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems. DIRECT transfer from NC MOD_SFIT_INTERSTAGE — identical process once surface is prepped and primed.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs after finish coat 1, before finish coat 2. Skipped for QT2 single-coat.

tasks.name: Interstage Inspection — Overhead
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat from ladder/scaffold for holidays, runs, sags, drips, and coverage defects. Overhead inspection requires good lighting — headlamp or portable light angled to reveal defects. Check T&G groove coverage on T&G board soffit.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays, drip marks
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection with raking light overhead. Mark all visible defects. Check T&G grooves for coverage.

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_INSPECT_COAT (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Intercoat Light Sand — QT4 Only
tasks.description: Light sand between finish coats with 220 grit overhead for mechanical adhesion and leveling. QT4 only — not required at QT3. Overhead sanding is slow and fatiguing. Dust falls directly onto painter — proper PPE mandatory.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand overhead. Remove nibs, drip marks, and defects. Uniform scratch pattern.

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_SAND_INTERCOAT (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Interstage Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during interstage inspection. Overhead brush detail work. Spot coat repaired areas to build film thickness before next full coat.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects found during inspection. Blend repairs.

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_TOUCHUP_REPAIR (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
tasks.description: Remove sanding dust from soffit surface before second coat. Tack cloth overhead. QT4 only (follows intercoat sand).
tasks.notes: All sanding dust removed before second finish coat.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_DUST_INTERCOAT (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Sand (QT4 only) → Touch up → Dust removal → Coat 2. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.

sop_modules.name: Finish — Coat 1 & Coat 2 Application (Brush/Roll or Spray) + Cut-In + T&G Brush-Back
sop_modules.description: Combined finish coat module for soffit repaint (coat 1 + coat 2). Brush/roll with extension pole is default (all soffit types). Spray eligible ONLY for non-vented soffit (FM-001). Cut-in at fascia/frieze junctions required for both brush/roll and spray. T&G groove brush-back required for spray + tg_board combination. Apply thin coats overhead to prevent sag. QT2 = coat 1 only (single finish). QT3/QT4 = coat 1 + interstage + coat 2. DIRECT transfer from NC finish modules (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_).

tasks.name: Cut-In at Fascia/Frieze Junctions — Coat 1
tasks.description: Brush cut-in at fascia-soffit and frieze-soffit junctions. Clean edge line where soffit meets adjacent trim. Overhead brush detail work. Required for both brush/roll and spray methods — spray alone cannot achieve clean junction lines.

quality_notes.QT4: Crisp, precise cut-in line at 3 ft viewing standard

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_CUTIN_FASCIA_1 (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Overhead Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by roller with extension pole for open field, brush for T&G grooves and edge detail. Thin coats overhead to prevent sag and drips (RISK-SFIT-006). Back-brush immediately after rolling to work paint into surface and catch drips. Default method for ALL vented soffits.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage overhead. No drips or sags.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform coverage. Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge overhead. Work T&G grooves with brush.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform appearance. No visible roller marks at 6 ft. T&G grooves fully coated.

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_FINISH_1_BRUSH_ROLL (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Overhead Application (Non-Vented Only)
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by airless spray overhead. NON-VENTED SOFFIT ONLY (FM-001). Lower pressure settings for overhead. Tight fan pattern (413-515 tip) for controlled application. On T&G board soffit: brush-back grooves after spray pass while wet.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build overhead. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft.

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_FINISH_1_SPRAY (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: T&G Groove Brush-Back After Spray — Coat 1
tasks.description: Brush paint into tongue-and-groove board joints after spray pass while coating is wet. Spray alone does not penetrate T&G groove channels — brush work is required even on non-vented T&G board soffit. Two-person operation: sprayer leads, brusher follows within 30-60 seconds.
tasks.notes: All groove channels must have full coverage. Follow sprayer within 30-60 seconds.
tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_TG_BRUSH_BACK_1 (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Cut-In at Fascia/Frieze Junctions — Coat 2
tasks.description: Brush cut-in at fascia-soffit and frieze-soffit junctions for second coat. Final appearance coat — precision matters.

quality_notes.QT3: Straight, consistent cut-in line. Final coat.
quality_notes.QT4: Crisp, precise cut-in line at 3 ft viewing standard. Final appearance coat.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Overhead Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by roller with extension pole and brush detail overhead. Thin coats to prevent sag. Final appearance coat. Default method for ALL vented soffits. QT3/QT4 only — QT2 skipped (single coat).

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. Maintain wet edge overhead.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform appearance. No visible roller marks at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_FINISH_2_BRUSH_ROLL (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Overhead Application (Non-Vented Only)
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by airless spray overhead. NON-VENTED SOFFIT ONLY. Final appearance coat. QT3/QT4 only.

quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

tasks.name: T&G Groove Brush-Back After Spray — Coat 2
tasks.description: Brush paint into T&G groove joints after spray pass for second coat. Same technique as coat 1. Final coat — all grooves must have full coverage.
tasks.notes: All groove channels fully coated. Follow sprayer within 30-60 seconds. Final appearance — no missed grooves.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Coat 1: Cut-in at fascia/frieze junctions → Spray or roll open field → T&G brush-back (spray + T&G only). QT2 stops after coat 1. → Interstage module (QT3/QT4) → Coat 2: Cut-in → Spray or roll → T&G brush-back.

sop_modules.name: Cleanup — Final Inspection, Touch-Up, Vent Unmask, Protection Teardown, Equipment Clean, Site Cleanup, Customer Walkthrough
sop_modules.description: Full cleanup module for exterior soffit repaint. Final walkthrough inspection and touch-up (merged from NC MOD_SFIT_FINAL_INSPECT). Vent opening unmask (RP-specific). Protection material teardown (landscape, hardscape, fixtures, fascia masking). Equipment cleaning. Site debris cleanup. Customer walkthrough (RP-specific — repaint work requires client sign-off and explanation of maintenance recommendations).

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection — Overhead
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect finished soffit from ground level and ladder as needed. Check coverage, consistency, edge lines at fascia/frieze junctions, T&G groove coverage, drip marks, and vent condition (vented soffit). Verify no overspray on adjacent fascia, siding, or fixtures.

quality_notes.QT2: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for misses and drip marks.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check all elevations. Verify T&G groove coverage.
quality_notes.QT4: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard. Raking light check on primary elevations. Verify edge line quality.

tasks.transfer_source: DIRECT from TSK_SFIT_FINAL_INSPECT (re-keyed TSK_SFIT_ to TSK_SFRP_)

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up — Overhead
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Overhead detail work from ladder/scaffold.

quality_notes.QT2: Fix obvious misses and drip marks
quality_notes.QT4: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft standard.

tasks.name: Remove Vent Opening Masking (Vented Soffit Only)

tasks.name: Clean Equipment

tasks.name: Customer Walkthrough
tasks.description: Walk soffit areas with homeowner. Inspect finish quality from ground level, verify vent function (vented soffit), confirm coverage and sheen consistency, confirm satisfaction. Address any touch-up requests on the spot. Provide maintenance recommendations: mildew-resistant paint extends coating life on sheltered soffit surfaces. RP-specific — repaint work requires client sign-off.

sop_modules.name: Lead-Safe RRP Exterior Containment (Shared Module)
sop_modules.description: Shared exterior lead-safe RRP module. Conditional on PS_EXT_META.FLAG.PRE_1978 = true and positive lead test. Per-elevation setup: 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745. Soffit is HIGH RISK for lead dust — overhead scraping sends paint chips and dust directly downward via gravity onto the crew and ground below. Wider containment than vertical wall work due to overhead debris spread. Shared across all exterior RP specs. This module is NOT owned by this spec — it is a shared module referenced by all exterior RP specs.

tasks.name: Lead Screening Test (XRF or Swab)
tasks.description: Perform lead test at representative soffit areas per elevation. XRF preferred; lead swab test acceptable. Test at minimum 2 locations per elevation. Soffit on pre-1978 homes commonly has lead paint.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. Results gate all subsequent RRP tasks and 2.0x prep modifier (FAC_SFRP_RRP).
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: RRP Exterior Containment Setup (Per Elevation)
tasks.description: Install 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule. WIDER than standard wall containment for overhead work — scraping debris spreads further when falling from eave height. Secure edges with weights or stakes. Install warning signage. Restrict area to certified RRP personnel only. Per-elevation setup.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. 6-mil poly minimum per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: RRP Wet Scraping Method
tasks.description: Wet-scrape method for lead paint removal on soffit. Mist surface with water before scraping to minimize dust generation. All scraping debris falls into containment below. Overhead wet scraping is especially critical — dry scraping overhead creates a shower of lead dust directly onto the crew below. EPA RRP requirement when disturbing lead paint.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Applied per SF. RRP doubles prep time on scraping tasks (2.0x modifier captured in FAC_SFRP_RRP). Overhead soffit wet scraping is the slowest RRP prep task.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
tasks.description: HEPA vacuum all soffit surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance to capture lead-contaminated dust. Required by EPA RRP Rule. Overhead HEPA vacuuming is awkward — dust falls into vacuum operator's face.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Applied per SF. Required after EVERY sanding/scraping disturbance — not just once.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

tasks.name: RRP Exterior Containment Teardown (Per Elevation)
tasks.description: Remove containment poly, fold inward to capture debris, bag for lead-safe disposal. Verify cleaning standard per EPA (visual + wet wipe test on hard surfaces, HEPA vacuum on soil). Per-elevation teardown.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. Must pass EPA cleaning verification standard before removing containment.
tasks.transfer_source: Shared RRP module

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Lead screen first → Containment setup (per elevation) → All paint disturbance tasks use wet methods within containment → HEPA vacuum after each disturbance → Containment teardown (per elevation, after all work complete on that elevation).

round_configurations.name: 2 Finish Coats Only (No Prime, GOOD Condition)
round_configurations.description: Most common RP round for soffit — GOOD is the dominant condition due to sheltered location. Skip prime when adhesion verified and existing paint is sound. Cosmetic refresh or color change.

round_configurations.name: 1 Finish Coat Only (Economy QT2, GOOD Condition)
round_configurations.description: Economy single-coat soffit RP on sound paint. Minimum viable scope.

round_configurations.name: State-Driven Prime + 2 Finish Coats (FAIR/POOR Condition)
round_configurations.description: Standard RP round for soffit with chalking, failing paint, or peeling. Prime coat is state-driven (chalk-binding for chalking, acrylic stain-block for failing/peeling) + material-specific on exposed areas.

round_configurations.name: State-Driven Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Economy QT2, FAIR/POOR Condition)
round_configurations.description: Economy RP with prime needed. Single finish coat on primed surface.

task_count_summary.reconciliation_note: Research projected 46 tasks (24 DIRECT + 8 MODIFIED + 19 RP_NEW - 5 NOT_APPLICABLE). This spec actualizes 46 spec-owned TSK_SFRP_* tasks + 5 shared TSK_RRP_EXT_* tasks = 51 total across all 8 modules. All 24 NC DIRECT transfers re-keyed from TSK_SFIT_* to TSK_SFRP_* per RP convention. 5 NC tasks NOT_APPLICABLE (SEAL_CUT_EDGES, SPOT_PRIME_KNOTS, PRIME_VINYL_SPRAY, PRIME_ALKALI_SPRAY, CAULK_JOINTS). Research RP_NEW overlap resolved: DEGLOSS_SCUFF counted as MODIFIED only; LANDSCAPE_PROTECT and HARDSCAPE_PROTECT counted as DIRECT_REKEYED only; RRP_CONTAINMENT_SETUP/TEARDOWN absorbed into shared MOD_RRP_EXT_CONTAINMENT.

module_sequence.notes: RRP containment (if applicable) after general setup but before assessment. Assessment drives prep/prime task activation. Wash is first task in PREP (merged from resolution's standalone WASH module). Interstage runs between finish coat 1 and coat 2 (skipped for QT2 single-coat). Final inspect and customer walkthrough merged into CLEANUP. Elevation strategy: work one elevation at a time to minimize protection setup/teardown cycles.
